_comment: Copy to raythink.config.json (gitignored) and adjust as needed. Shared settings applied to every Raythink camera; the config profile (LAN/Cellular) and the addressing (static octet, or DHCP) are chosen in the UI per camera (one camera at a time).
_comment_generations: Raythink ships two generations with incompatible control APIs, told apart automatically by probing which one answers (firmware 'B1.2.01.01.15, 2026-05-14' = newer/REST, '1.000.General 00.0.T, build: 2025-04-09' = older/RPC2). Everything below is shared by both EXCEPT 'profiles', where each generation needs its own exported config file.
_comment_pw: Factory login is admin/admin; the tool changes it to new_password. A re-run of a half-configured camera falls back to new_password automatically.

static._comment: The camera moves to subnet_prefix.<octet> as the LAST step (the connection drops; the tool reconnects on the new address and renews the laptop's DHCP lease). The octet comes from the address mode chosen in the UI: 'fixed' = every camera gets fixed_octet (for projects where each site takes ONE camera, so every unit ships with the same default configuration), 'cycle' = auto 30 -> 31 -> ... -> 50 -> 30 (for sites taking several), 'manual' = type it per camera. 'dhcp' is the fourth mode and assigns nothing. default_mode sets which the UI opens on; the operator's choice is then remembered in ip_state.json across cameras and restarts.

dhcp._comment: Used by the UI's DHCP mode, where the camera keeps the address its own DHCP server hands out instead of a bench-assigned static one. Because nothing here chose that address, the tool finds the camera again by MAC: it sweeps scan_subnets (CIDR) for up to lease_timeout seconds, then verifies on whatever it landed on. List the subnet(s) the lease can come from — the bench subnet first, then the factory one (a camera that never gets a lease falls back to its previous static address). This PC must hold an address on the subnet the camera lands on: ARP is link-local, so a device is only findable by MAC on a subnet you are on. lease_timeout must cover the camera rebooting, taking a lease AND starting its web server — much longer than a static move, where only the address changes.

_comment_profiles: Each profile is a config JSON exported from a reference camera (Setup > System > Export), stored under config/profiles/ (paths are relative to config/). The two generations export incompatible files — the older one a map of config tables replayed one setConfig at a time, the newer one a set of sections uploaded whole — so one profile key names one file PER GENERATION: {"rpc2": "...", "rest": "..."}. A plain string still means the older generation only, so a bench that has not met a new camera yet needs no change here.
_comment_profiles_sanitize: Run a raw export through 'python3 raythink_configure.py --sanitize-profile export.json -o config/profiles/v2/lan.json' before committing it. That drops the reference camera's own address (which would move the next unit mid-run, since the tool addresses the camera LAST) and the station password, which a newer camera's export carries in PLAINTEXT under OnvifUser. The tool sets the address, NTP and the ONVIF credential itself, after the import.
_comment_timeouts: import_reboot_timeout: seconds to wait for the camera to come back if a config import reboots it. ip_move_timeout: seconds to wait for the camera to answer on its new static IP.
